basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Vocavitque Dominus Deus Adam, et dixit ei: Ubi es? Non utique ignorando quaesivit, sed'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Vocavitque Dominus Deus Adam, et dixit ei: Ubi es? Non utique ignorando quaesivit, sed increpando admonuit, ut attenderet ubi esset in quo Deus non esset. Jam enim quia de arbore vetita comederat, mortuus erat morte animae, cum eam deseruisse vita sua dicitur. « Et hoc sane ad aliquam pertinet significationem, quod sicut praeceptum viro datum est per quem perveniret ad feminam; ita vir prior interrogatur. Praeceptum enim a Domino per virum usque ad feminam: peccatum autem a diabolo per feminam usque ad virum. Haec mysticis significationibus plena sunt, non id agentibus in quibus facta sunt, sed de his id agente potentissima sapientia Dei non autem nunc significata referamus, sed gesta defendimus. »
